display.title: Episode 377: The Flickering Flame (Sefiras HaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Sefirah show about respect, the value of time and humility: a shoemaker's lamp teaches a great tzaddik that while the flame burns we can still repair, and Har Sinai teaches us to be humble.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 11 Iyar 5749, during Sefiras HaOmer, with no music because of the Sefirah mourning. Uncle Yossi recalls how Rabbi Akiva's students were punished for not respecting one another, and urges respect for parents, teachers and friends, seeing the good in others, and pursuing peace, so that we can ask Hashem 'Ad Mosai' with a clear conscience. He explains that counting Sefirah teaches us that every day is precious and each day should be better than the last. A young yeshiva boy leads the Shema. In the story, the tzaddik Rabbi Yisroel, caught in a snowstorm, is welcomed into the home of an old shoemaker who is still working past midnight because he put too much oil in his lamp: 'As long as the light is burning, one can still repair.' The tzaddik hears a lesson about teshuvah. Before Shavuos, Uncle Yossi teaches why Moshe Rabbeinu, the humblest of men, received the Torah, and why it was given on Har Sinai, the lowest mountain. The show ends with news of the Lag BaOmer outing in Prospect Park and Shabbos candle times.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: use every day to grow, and while life's flame still burns it is never too late to do teshuvah. Be humble like Moshe Rabbeinu.
